# FDG3003

> DO capitalize both characters of two-character acronyms, except the first word of a camel-cased identifier.

Framework Design Guidelines, 3rd edition, section 3.1.2 Capitalizing Acronyms.

## How it is checked

- Check: fdg (partial coverage)
- Diagnostics: FDG3003
- Automatic fix: no
- Severity: library warning, application warning, test none
- Status: draft

Message: Capitalize both characters of the two-character acronym '{1}' in '{0}'

FDG3003 and FDG3004 report, in the names that externally visible declarations choose (namespaces, types, members, parameters and type parameters; not overrides or interface implementations), a word that is one of the acronyms chapter 3 itself names and that is cased otherwise than the book shows: IO and UI in capitals; Html, Xml, Rgb and Argb with only the first letter capitalized. The first word of a parameter name is left to FDG3005, and the I prefix of an interface and the T prefix of a type parameter are not part of the first word. Other acronyms are not checked, because the book gives no longer list.

## From the book

```csharp
System.IO
System.Threading.IOCompletionCallback
public void StartIO(Stream ioStream)
```
